newsitem.title: UK: Former MTM executives sentenced for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Former MTM executives sentenced for fraud.

text.p: Richard Lines, founder and former chairman of fine chemicals company MTM Plc, was sentenced on Monday to two years in prison after being found guilty of false accounting and making misleading statements.
MTM's former finance director Thomas Baxter received a six month sentence in the same case.

The trial stemmed from an investigation by the Serious Fraud Office (SFO) and North Yorkshire Police fraud squad into Wetherbey-based MTM, now known as Meristem Plc, after 250 million stg was wiped off the company's share price in 1992.
During the trial, the prosecution said Lines and Baxter had "cooked the books" of the firm to make it appear much more profitable than it really was.
The prosecution also alleged that Lines and Baxter had lied to investors and analysts about the trading position of the company during a set of meetings in March 1992.
Sentencing Lines, Judge Geoffrey Grigson said: "You have persistently and deliberately been proved to be dishonest."
Lines was also banned from being a company director for five years.
Sentencing Baxter, the Judge told him he had failed in his duty as a Chartered Accountant and disqualified him from being a company manager for two years.
